_comment: What's new in Golden Eye, shown in Settings → Updates. Newest first. Written for the people using the dashboard, not as commit messages. Add an entry in the same commit as the change it describes. area: SEO | Reports | Onboarding | Tasks | Security | Data. action: only when something has to be run or deployed before it works.

updates.title: Competitor numbers fixed, directories hidden
updates.what: Fixed: a competitor who isn't in Google's top 100 was being counted as ranking #100, so every comparison said we were ahead. Midas showed "ahead on 14, behind on 0" against all five competitors when four of them don't rank for those searches at all. They now count as not ranking. "Who owns this market" also hides directories and manufacturers (Yelp, Houzz, Trex, booking widgets) by default, with a button to show them, so the list shows the local businesses worth tracking.
updates.action: Re-run supabase/sql/seo_competitors.sql (it also clears the bad rows), then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Competitors
updates.what: The SEO tab now tracks the other companies ranking for a client's searches. Admin side: one line per competitor (how many page-1 spots they hold, where we're ahead, where they are), a search-by-search grid, and "who owns this market" — every site in Google's top 10, sorted by how many of the client's cities it appears in. The client's Organic Search tab gets a plain "How you compare" section: how many shared searches they're ahead on, counts only, no jargon.
updates.note: 3Sixty now tracks Backyard Builders Utah, Blackrock Decks, TC Decks Utah, Eremos Decks and Quality Decking of Utah — chosen from SE Ranking's own top-10 data, not a guess. Competitor ranks are organic only; SE Ranking doesn't report their Google Maps spot. Data starts at the next daily check, since competitor history never backfills.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/seo_competitors.sql, then supabase/sql/rename_client.sql, then deploy seranking-sync

updates.title: Rankings by city
updates.what: For clients tracked in more than one city, Tracked Keywords has a "Rankings from" picker. All cities shows each keyword's best spot, with a "N cities" button that opens that keyword's rank in every city. Pick one city to see the whole table, and the wrong-page alerts, from there. Alerts now name the city where the wrong page ranks.
updates.note: Also fixed: a keyword's ranking page could come from a different city than its rank. It now comes from the city with the best rank.

updates.title: Wrong-page alerts
updates.what: The SEO tab now warns when Google ranks a different page than the one you set as the target in SE Ranking, for example the blog list showing up instead of the deck repair page. Flagged keywords get a warning icon, and a summary above Tracked Keywords lists every mismatch with the page that is ranking and the page that should be.
updates.note: 3Sixty is set up for this: 5 cities tracked (Eagle Mountain, Lehi, Saratoga Springs, American Fork, Draper) and 53 keywords, each with a target page.

updates.title: Keywords follow your SE Ranking list
updates.what: Keywords you remove in SE Ranking now drop off the SEO tab and reports on the next sync (their history is kept). Each keyword's target page is also brought in from SE Ranking, ready for the wrong-page alerts.

updates.title: A tidier SEO tab
updates.what: The SEO Changelog, Top Pages and Tracked Keywords now show their first three rows, with a View all button to open the rest. A list you open stays open while you change the date range.

updates.title: This Updates page
updates.what: Every change to Golden Eye in plain English, newest first, with anything still needing a SQL run or deploy marked Action needed. The tab shows a count of what's new since you last looked.

updates.title: Weekly reports now include real SEO results
updates.what: A report for an SEO client gets an Organic Search section built from the same numbers their SEO tab shows: visits and leads from Google, jobs they reported closing from Google, which searches moved up, searches sitting on page 2, and the articles and fixes that went live that week. Small numbers stay plain counts instead of being spun as percentages.
updates.note: Also fixed: the "period before" comparison was one day longer than the period being reported, which slightly inflated every prior-period figure here and on the SEO tab.

updates.title: Every Make automation now requires a secret
updates.what: Make webhook links are public, and anyone holding one could make Golden Eye text a client, draft an email, or overwrite an ad approval. All five now check a shared secret first, and the two that send texts look up contacts by exact phone match so one reminder can never reach several people.
updates.note: This also uncovered that admin alerts for client requests had never actually fired: the scenario was filtering on the wrong field. Fixed, so onboarding-complete and help requests now text you.

updates.title: Hide a task from the client
updates.what: Tick "Hide from client" on any task and it stays on your board, marked Hidden, but never shows in their portal, their weekly work summary or their report. Hidden is enforced in the database, not just on screen.

updates.title: Forms you build inside Golden Eye
updates.what: A step can now be a set of questions answered right in the portal, with no GHL form and no Make scenario behind it. Write the questions in Templates, mark any as required, and show a question only for clients with an existing site or a new build. Answers appear on the client's page with a Copy button, ready to paste into Cuppa.

updates.title: SEO onboarding steps, and hiding a step until it's ready
updates.what: The SEO Growth steps are in: an intake form and a Google access video for the client, and seven setup tasks for us. The eye button on any step hides it from clients, so a step can be drafted before its video or form exists.

updates.title: Tasks that tick themselves off
updates.what: Setup tasks close on their own once Golden Eye can see the work is done: the ad account is saved, spend is flowing, Search Console is syncing, the first article auto-logged, the first website lead arrived. Each carries a note saying why it closed. A lightning bolt marks which tasks work this way.

updates.title: Onboarding follows what each client actually bought
updates.what: Clients get the steps for their add-ons and website situation, nothing else. An SEO-only client never sees Facebook steps. Adding SEO to a long-standing client brings back Get Started with just the SEO steps, raises our SEO tasks when they finish, and doesn't re-announce their original onboarding.
updates.action: Run supabase/sql/service_onboarding.sql, then the trigger file and its tests.

updates.title: Services, step tags and a client preview in Templates
updates.what: Templates → Services manages the add-ons. Every onboarding step and stage checklist item can be tagged by add-on and website situation, and Preview a Client shows exactly what someone with, say, Ads + SEO and an existing site would get. Add/Edit Client gained add-on checkboxes and a website dropdown.

updates.title: The client SEO tab
updates.what: SEO clients now have a tab written for people who don't know SEO: what it did for their business, how far they've come since starting, a traffic chart marked with the work we did, their target searches in plain language, and what's next. A return-per-dollar figure appears only once it's genuinely positive.

updates.title: Articles log themselves
updates.what: Publishing on Webflow, Wix, Sanity or a GitHub-based site records itself in the SEO changelog, with markers on the traffic chart showing when each went live. Setup is about a minute per client from the SEO tab. Midas's 42 articles and 3Sixty's 55 posts were backfilled.

updates.title: Almost Page 1, and map-pack rankings counted properly
updates.what: The admin SEO tab lists searches sitting on page 2, which are the best content targets. Keyword rankings now count a map-pack placement as ranking, so a local client in the map pack no longer reads as "not ranking".

updates.title: Check-ins ask where each job came from
updates.what: The weekly check-in splits closed jobs and revenue by source: Google or your website, Facebook or Instagram ads, referrals, or other. Totals still work exactly as before, and the Google row is what powers the return figures on the SEO tab.

updates.title: Reports explain the work in the client's words
updates.what: "What We're Working On" is always included, with planned to-dos rewritten as plain language rather than pasted task titles, and no internal due dates or assignees. Notes you type are saved with the report, the summary reads casually, and a week with no prior spend is treated as a fresh baseline instead of compared to nothing.
